passage: Mother had gone to her sister's for a week and left Saurabh in charge of the seedlings on the balcony. Saurabh was thrilled. Morning: a full mug on each pot. After lunch: another. At dusk: another. "More water, faster growth," he told the seedlings. On the fifth day the leaves went yellow and floppy and the soil smelled sour. He rang his neighbour, Preeti Aunty, who tipped a pot and showed him the soft brown roots. "Too much love," she said gently. Half the seedlings were beyond saving, and Saurabh could not look at the empty pots.

qa.q: How often a day did Saurabh water the seedlings?
qa.a: He watered them three times a day: morning, after lunch and at dusk.

qa.q: What was Saurabh feeling when the seedlings' leaves went yellow?
qa.a: Worried and puzzled, since he had tried so hard and things had got worse.

qa.q: What could Saurabh do next time, and why?
qa.a: He could touch the soil first and water only when it feels dry, because roots need air as well as water.

qa.q: How does Preeti Aunty see Saurabh's mistake?
qa.a: Preeti Aunty is kind about it, calling it too much love, and sees eagerness rather than carelessness.

grounding: A child waters seedlings several times a day, thinking more means faster growth, and the roots rot.

passage: On their ninth-floor balcony in Gurugram, Jatin had planted six bean seeds in a plastic tray for a school project. The first two sprouts appeared on Monday. Jatin was so excited that he watered them before school, after school, after dinner and once more before bed. "More water, faster beans," he told his friend Divyansh on the phone. The tray had no holes. By the next week the soil smelled sour and stayed dark and wet. The leaves turned yellow at the edges, then the stems flopped over the side. When Jatin lifted one out, the root was brown and mushy, not white. He sat on the balcony floor holding it for a long time.

qa.q: How many bean seeds did Jatin plant?
What was Jatin feeling when he watered the beans four times a day?
qa.a: He was excited and eager, believing that more water meant faster beans.

qa.q: What else could Jatin try with new seeds?
qa.a: He could use a tray with holes and water only when a finger in the soil feels dry.

qa.q: What would change if the tray had drainage holes?
qa.a: Extra water would drain away, so the roots might have had air and not rotted so quickly.

grounding: A child overwaters seedlings out of eagerness until the roots rot and the plants yellow and droop.

passage:
"Rekha, you watered them again?"
"Only a little, Dadaji. Third time today."
"Third? The soil's already black."
"But they grow so slowly! More water, more growing."
Hemant bent and pressed the soil. Water oozed up round his thumb. "Look. They can't drink any more. They're drowning."
"Plants can't drown."
Five days later:
"Dadaji! The tomato leaves are yellow. And they're all bent over!"
Hemant slid a seedling out of the pot. The roots were brown and soft. "See? Roots need air too. We gave them a swimming pool."
"I only wanted them to grow fast." Rekha's lip wobbled.
"I know, beta. We'll start again. This time, the finger test first."

qa.q: How many times had Rekha watered that day?
What does Rekha's wobbling lip show?
qa.a: She felt upset and guilty that her eagerness had hurt the seedlings.

qa.q: What else could Rekha have done when growth seemed slow?
qa.a: She could have checked the soil first and measured the plants weekly, so small progress would show without extra water.

qa.q: How does Hemant respond to the mistake?
qa.a: Gently: he shows her the roots, explains why, and offers to start again with the finger test.

grounding: A child waters tomato seedlings several times a day to speed them up, and the roots rot until the leaves yellow and droop.
